clue.text: Person with family has a large eye

definitions.note: describes the thing rather than naming it: a blunt needle with a big eye for threading tape

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or body
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by relatives happens to have one unusually big eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: rather than a synonym, it tells you what the object has, the big threading eye of this kind of needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a thick blunt needle with an oversized eye for drawing tape or ribbon through hems.

clue.text: Tory leader's intellect is found in container by a priest under hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest is written under the first piece

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain or hill

indicators.note: found in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a jar is a container
mind means intellect
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief's brains turn out to be kept in a jar beside a cleric below a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the rest below the hill. ELI is the Old Testament priest who trained Samuel; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli led the Conservative Party and was twice British Prime Minister.

clue.text: See 1
I severely criticise religion

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to attacking faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith of Muslims, founded by Muhammad.

clue.text: China, say, for "good girl" plates

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
she stands for any girl or woman
L-plates are the plates a British learner driver displays, giving L and L

explanation.surface: A piece of china is offered as a reward for a well-behaved girl, the plates being her prize.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers must show red L-plates front and back, so 'plates' gives LL. 'China, say' looks like one phrase, but 'say' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china, or eggshell porcelain, is an extremely thin translucent kind of fine china.

clue.text: Epithet for Austen hero taking me and Ellen out

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered and set out anew

explanation.surface: A description of a novel's hero who goes out with the speaker and a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link, not fodder. Elizabeth tells Darcy in Pride and Prejudice he might have behaved 'in a more gentlemanlike manner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Bennet's reproach to Darcy makes this adjective, meaning befitting a gentleman, his famous tag.

clue.text: Awfully unsteady article giving time for the best cakes?

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wobbly item proves a fine occasion for cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link. UNSTEADY rearranges to SUNDAYTE, with A on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Sunday afternoon meal is traditionally when the finest homemade cakes come out.

clue.text: Flag officer?

definitions.meaning: a banner, especially one flown by a ship to show nationality
a junior commissioned officer, historically the one carrying the colours

explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a naval flag and also a lowest-rank commissioned officer, especially in the US Navy.

clue.text: Inexpert folk, handicapped, retaining unknown name

parts.note: lame means impaired in walking
algebra uses y for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Unskilled people, disabled, keep a nameless stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are non-professionals lacking specialist knowledge, so they are inexpert.

clue.text: German as a language has a certain twang

indicators.note: the phrase before it has, or contains, the run of letters wanted

explanation.surface: A remark that the German tongue sounds somewhat through the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'germaN AS A Language'. 'has' looks like a verb joining subject to definition but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice, and a nasal is a sound made through the nose.

clue.text: Study in selective education by …

definitions.note: the whole clue points at a novel by the puzzle's statesman, a study of young men educated at Eton

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
GS is short for grammar school, the selective state school in Britain

explanation.surface: The opening of a sentence about research into selective schooling, trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: A British grammar school selects pupils by exam, hence GS. The ellipsis leaves 'by' hanging so the solver supplies the author, the statesman at 1/2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Coningsby is Disraeli's 1844 political novel, opening at Eton, a study of the young Tory generation.

clue.text: Anxiety returns after tea with illumination that isn't scheduled

indicators.note: after puts the reversed worry behind the tea

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: returns means the word for worry is read backwards

parts.note: fret means worry or anxiety
light means illumination

explanation.surface: A traveller's nerves come back after a cuppa in an unplanned glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'returns' turns FRET into TERF.
explanation.definitionFit: A charter flight is hired for a particular trip, as opposed to a regular scheduled service.

clue.text: Flying medal for everyone to wake up

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning relating to wings, hence to flying
MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A gallantry medal awarded to an entire unit gets everybody out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' is not an anagram signal here: ALAR, wing-related, supplies the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone or hotel alarm call is the request that rouses you from sleep, a wake-up call.

clue.text: Old English fish

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic people whose name gave England, an early English settler
to fish with rod and line

explanation.definitionFit: An Angle was one of the early Germanic English, and to angle is to fish with a hook.

clue.text: Bar sinister means one left … to scarper with single friend

definitions.note: a heraldic band said to mark a bastard line, standing for the state of being born out of wedlock

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
leg it is British slang for to run off or scarper
I as a single, the numeral one
mate is a British word for a friend

explanation.surface: A heraldic symbol is explained by someone running off with an unattached companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' and the ellipsis are links. The bar sinister is popularly held to show illegitimate descent in a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar sinister on a coat of arms is popularly taken to signal birth outside marriage.

clue.text: Pleased to get jewel from 2's opponent

parts.note: glad means pleased
a stone is a gem or jewel

explanation.surface: Happy to receive a gem from a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'from' are links. 2 is DISRAELI, whose great Liberal rival this was.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone, the Liberal leader, was Disraeli's long-standing parliamentary adversary.

clue.text: Opposed to agricultural land in which "i" is used for "x"?

parts.note: v for versus means against or opposed to

indicators.note: in which says the letter goes inside the land

parts.note: arable land is ploughed for crops

explanation.surface: An algebra lesson against farmland where one letter stands in for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is used for' is link material. x in algebra is the classic unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra x is the typical symbol for an unknown changeable quantity, a variable.

clue.text: Complaint of above girl to Welshman in play

parts.note: flu is an illness or complaint
Ellen is the girl named in the clue above, 5 down

explanation.surface: A girl's ailment is passed to a Welsh character in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'to' are links; 'above girl' points back to Ellen in 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluellen is the comic Welsh captain in Shakespeare's Henry V.

clue.text: Film star Stan grasps note on a state

indicators.note: grasps means one name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy
NB, nota bene, means note well
Cal is a short form for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A comic actor clutches a memo about an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: NB (nota bene, Latin for note well) and CAL for California are standard abbreviations; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was a Hollywood star of the 1940s, famous opposite Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Early stage reached by more dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters move about into new order

explanation.surface: A beginning arrived at by more dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reached' is a link; BY and MORE rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism at its first stage of development, so anything in embryo is at an early stage.

clue.text: Easy wind to block

definitions.meaning: the word that goes before block in a cinder building block

explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is an easy task, a light wind, and the cinders in a breeze block.

clue.text: The pity may follow the customs

definitions.meaning: the phrase that comes before 'the pity' in the idiom of regret
the accepted social conventions of a community

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'more's the pity' puts this word before 'the pity', and mores are a society's customs.

clue.text: Rejected or retained, Adelaide is displaying pointlessly

indicators.note: displaying suggests the letters are set out in a fresh arrangement
without a point, so one compass point (E for east) is dropped from the city and verb

explanation.surface: An Australian city puts something on show in a meaningless way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' removes one E (a compass point) from ADELAIDE IS, and 'displaying' rearranges ADLAIDEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid aside may be dropped as rejected, or put by and kept for later, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Gangway is swamped by liquor

indicators.note: swamped by means surrounded by the drink

parts.note: ale is a malt liquor

explanation.surface: A passage is flooded with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passageway between seats, a gangway.

clue.text: Regret last resting place for Poe's crime scene

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a morgue holds the dead before burial

explanation.surface: Lamenting a final resting place for a writer's murder setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Murders in the Rue Morgue, by Edgar Allan Poe, is set in that Paris street.

clue.text: 2's girl heard to make a profit (say)

indicators.note: heard tells us we want a word that sounds the same as another

parts.note: taken as heard, a profit is a prophet, and a female prophet is a sibyl

explanation.surface: A girl apparently known for earning money, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link. 'profit' read by ear is 'prophet'; a prophetess is a SIBYL, which sounds like Disraeli's novel and heroine Sybil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil, or The Two Nations, is Disraeli's 1845 novel, named after its heroine.

clue.text: No time for letter home — turn to breaking 4 for this

indicators.note: turn tells us to rearrange the letters once the hour is taken away

parts.note: hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A busy person has no time to write home and turns to cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes HR out of LETTER HOME; 'turn' rearranges the rest. The definition refers to 4-across: you break eggshells to make this.
explanation.definitionFit: You cannot make an omelette without breaking eggs, so cracked shells are the price of this dish.

clue.text: Humble setter gripped by churchman

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
the setter refers to themself, giving me

explanation.surface: A modest crossword compiler is held by a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to humble or lower them in dignity.
